name: Dominican Republic
description: The Dominican Republic offers expats a vibrant Caribbean lifestyle with a significantly lower cost of living compared to North America and Europe. Its appeal lies in year-round warm weather, beautiful beaches, and a rich culture, making it an attractive destination for retirees, digital nomads, and entrepreneurs.
longdescription: Expat life in the Dominican Republic is characterized by a relaxed, outdoor-focused lifestyle, where beach trips and social gatherings are common. The country provides a diverse environment, from the bustling capital of Santo Domingo with its colonial zone, to serene beach towns like Las Terrenas and Cabarete. The economy benefits from strong tourism and growing sectors like finance and services, offering opportunities for working professionals and entrepreneurs. Dominicans are generally known for their warm hospitality and friendly nature, though adapting to a slower 'island time' and navigating bureaucracy can require patience. While the cost of living is affordable, especially for housing and local produce, challenges include unreliable electricity, chaotic traffic in major cities, and the need to learn Spanish for full integration. Expats can find well-equipped hospitals and quality healthcare at affordable prices.

visas.name: Dominican Republic Rentista Visa
visas.description: Residency for those with a regular passive income from investments, pensions, or other sources. One of the most accessible residency programs in the Caribbean.
benefits: Legal residency
Low income threshold ($1,500/month)
Path to permanent residency
Tax incentives for retirees
Warm Caribbean climate
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 3 years of legal residency, eligible to apply for permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport
Proof of $1,500/month income
Birth certificate (apostilled)
Police clearance (apostilled)
Medical certificate
Passport photos

visas.name: Dominican Republic Retirement Visa
visas.description: Special retirement residency (Law 171-07) offering significant tax benefits to foreign retirees including exemption from import duties on personal goods.
benefits: Import vehicle duty-free
Import household goods duty-free
Property purchase assistance
Tax exemptions
Year-round warm weather
visas.path_to_residency_description: Pathway to permanent residency after qualifying period.
required_documents: Passport
Proof of pension income ($1,500+/month)
Birth certificate
Police clearance
Medical exam
Passport photos

visas.name: Residency by Investment (Inversión)
visas.description: This visa is for foreign nationals who wish to obtain permanent residency in the Dominican Republic by making a significant economic investment in the country. It allows investors and their direct dependents to live, work, and study in the Dominican Republic.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign investor intending to make an economic investment of at least US$200,000 in local businesses or real estate in the Dominican Republic.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The program grants permanent residency directly. After 2 years of permanent residency, applicants are eligible to apply for naturalization (citizenship). Property owners investing US$200,000 may be eligible for naturalization in as little as 6 months of permanent residency. Fluency in Spanish and knowledge of Dominican culture are required for citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Initially valid for one year, then renewed for four-year periods. Investment requirements must continue to be met.
visas.tax_implications: The Dominican Republic operates a territorial tax system, meaning only local-source income is subject to taxation; foreign-source income is generally exempt. New residents are fully exempt from taxes on foreign-source investment income and gains for their first three years of residency. There may also be potential tax exemptions on real estate transfers (for the first purchase).
benefits: Ability to live, study, and work in the Dominican Republic.
Efficient processing times, typically within 45 business days for the residency card.
Eligibility for naturalization (citizenship) after a period of permanent residency, potentially as short as 6 months for property owners.
No minimum physical stay requirement to maintain residence status.
Inclusion of spouse and minor children under the same application.
required_documents: Valid passport (minimum 6 months validity)
Residence Visa (RS) issued by a Dominican consulate prior to entry (if applicable)
Application form for residency by investment
Letter from the authorized company (if applicable, endorsing the investor's inclusion in the program)
Certified proof of foreign investment issued by Pro-Dominicana (formerly CEI-RD)
Birth certificate (original, apostilled or legalized, and translated to Spanish if applicable)

Police clearance certificate (non-criminal record) from country of origin and any country of residence for the last 5 years (apostilled or legalized, and translated to Spanish if applicable; not required for minors)
Four (4) recent photographs (4x5 cm, front-facing, white background)
Proof of entry of foreign currency or physical/intangible assets into the Dominican Republic
Constitutive documents of the commercial society or authorization of branch operation (if applicable)
Notarized declaration of origin of funds
Marriage certificate or notarized declaration of free union (if applicable, legalized or apostilled, and translated to Spanish if applicable)
Copy of naturalization certificate (if acquired a nationality different from origin, certified, apostilled, and translated if applicable)
application_process_steps: Register the investment with Pro-Dominicana (Export and Investment Center of the Dominican Republic) to obtain the required investment certificate.
Gather all necessary personal and investment-related documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated where required.
Submit the complete application package to the Dirección General de Migración (DGM).
Undergo medical examinations as part of the residency application process.
Receive approval and the issuance of the permanent residence card.

visas.name: Residency for Retirees or Pensioners (Pensionado)
visas.description: This visa program is designed for foreign individuals who receive a stable monthly pension or retirement income from a foreign government, official body, or private company and wish to establish residence in the Dominican Republic. It offers a fast-tracked path to permanent residency and provides significant tax incentives for eligible retirees.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retirees or pensioners with a guaranteed monthly income from foreign sources, seeking to reside long-term in the Dominican Republic and benefit from tax exemptions.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The initial 'Pensionado' residency is granted for one year and is renewable. This program offers a fast-track to permanent residency, which can be obtained after a shorter period (e.g., 2 years) compared to the standard temporary residency route. After obtaining permanent residency, applicants may apply for Dominican citizenship without needing to waive their original nationality.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew the residency permit, the applicant must prove that the minimum US$1,500 monthly pension continues to be transferred to a local Dominican bank.
visas.tax_implications: Beneficiaries of this program receive significant tax incentives under Law 171-07. These include exemption from customs tariffs on household goods, partial tax exemption on motor vehicles, exemption from property transfer taxes for the first home, 50% reduction in mortgage taxes, 50% reduction in property taxes, exemption from taxes on dividends and interest from local or foreign sources, and a 50% reduction in capital gains tax under certain conditions. New residents are also fully exempt from taxes on foreign-source investment income and gains for their first three years of residency.
benefits: Expedited path to permanent residency, bypassing the standard temporary residency period.
Exemption from customs tariffs for household goods and personal items.
Partial tax exemption on motor vehicles.
Exemption from property transfer taxes on the first home purchase.
50% reduction in property taxes (where applicable) and mortgage taxes (if the lender is a regulated financial institution).
Exemption from taxes on dividends and interest earned locally or abroad.
50% reduction in capital gains tax, provided the retiree is the majority shareholder of a company not engaged in commercial or industrial activities.
required_documents: Application letter addressed to the Director General de Migración.
Completed residency application form (available on DGM portal).
Full passport copy with a minimum validity of one (1) year (some sources say 18 months).
Residency Visa (RS) obtained from a Dominican consulate in the applicant's country of origin or residence.
Original birth certificate, duly apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish if in another language.
Four (4) recent passport-size photographs (two frontal, two right profile, with white background).

Certificate of No Criminal Record from the country where the applicant has resided for the last five (5) years, duly apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish if in another language (not required for minors under 16).
Medical certification confirming no contagious diseases (initially a letter, followed by an in-country medical exam at a DGM-authorized clinic).
Official certification from a foreign government, official body, or private company confirming the applicant's pension.
Two (2) recent bank statements reflecting monthly pension deposits (apostilled).
Original bank reference letter from a Dominican bank where the applicant holds an account (not older than 6 months).
Marriage certificate, if applicable (apostilled or legalized and translated).
Divorce certificate, if applicable (apostilled or legalized and translated).
Affidavit of support for dependents (if applicable).
Copy of the entry stamp into the Dominican Republic.
Health insurance policy covering the applicant and any dependents.
All non-Spanish documents must be translated by a certified judicial translator in the Dominican Republic or by a Dominican consulate.
application_process_steps: Apply for a Residency Visa (RS) at the Dominican Consulate in your country of origin or legal residence, submitting required documentation.
Once the Residency Visa is granted, travel to the Dominican Republic within its 60-day validity period.
Upon arrival, submit the residency application to the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) with all required original documents and two sets of copies.
Undergo a mandatory medical examination at a DGM-approved clinic in the Dominican Republic.
After DGM approval, provide fingerprints and have a photo taken for the residency card.
Receive your initial residency card, which is typically valid for one year.

visas.name: Residency for Independent Means (Rentista)
visas.description: This program grants residency to foreign nationals who can demonstrate a stable and permanent passive income sourced from outside the Dominican Republic. It provides a pathway for individuals to live in the country without needing to engage in local employment, leveraging their foreign-generated wealth.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals with a consistent monthly passive income from international sources such as investments, company dividends, or property rentals.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This program offers a fast-track to permanent residency. After two years of holding permanent residency, applicants become eligible to apply for Dominican citizenship, provided they maintain the income requirements and demonstrate ties to the country, including an interview in Spanish.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the minimum passive income threshold and other terms of the visa.
visas.tax_implications: Beneficiaries of the Rentista visa fall under Law 171-07, which offers special incentives. The Dominican Republic operates on a territorial tax system, generally taxing only income generated within the country. This visa category provides exemptions from taxes on dividends and interest (local and foreign-generated) and a 50% exemption on real estate tax (IPI) for the first home purchased.
benefits: Fast-track to permanent residency for the applicant and immediate family.
Potential pathway to Dominican citizenship after two years of permanent residency.
Access to the Dominican Republic's territorial tax system, meaning only local income is taxed.
Exemption of taxes on dividends and interest, both local and foreign-generated.
50% exemption on real estate tax (IPI) for the first home purchased.
Low cost of living compared to many Western countries.
required_documents: Application letter addressed to the Director General of Migration.
Residency application form completed via the DGM services portal.
Complete passport copy with a minimum validity of 18 months.
Current Residence Visa (RS) issued by a Dominican consulate.
Original birth certificate, apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish.
Four recent 2x2 inch photographs (two front, two right profile, white background, no jewelry or accessories).
Federal criminal record certificate from the country of origin or where the applicant has resided in the last 5 years, apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish.

Documentation proving stable and permanent passive income from abroad (e.g., certification of company ownership/shares, financial statements, investment certificates, rental contracts, bank certifications, etc.), apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish.
Original receipt of payment for medical examinations (to be performed at institutions authorized by the DGM in the Dominican Republic).
Marriage certificate (if applicable), apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish.
Bank letter confirming a local Dominican bank account.
Health insurance policy from a local Dominican insurer (e.g., Seguros Reservas).
application_process_steps: Obtain a Residency Visa (RS) from the Dominican Consulate in your country of origin or legal residence.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish where necessary.
Submit the visa application to the consulate and pay the corresponding fee.
Upon visa approval, travel to the Dominican Republic.
Within 30 days of arrival, present to the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) to formalize your residency application.
Undergo mandatory medical examinations at institutions authorized by the DGM in the Dominican Republic.

visas.name: Temporary Workers Visa (VTT - Visa de Trabajador Temporero)
visas.description: The Temporary Workers Visa (VTT - Visa de Trabajador Temporero) is issued to foreign nationals who have secured a formal employment contract with a legally established company in the Dominican Republic. This visa permits entry into the country for the purpose of temporary employment.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign nationals who have a confirmed job offer from a Dominican Republic-based company and intend to work in the country temporarily.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Temporary Workers Visa (VTT) is the prerequisite for applying for a Temporary Worker Permit (Permiso de Trabajador Temporero) or Temporary Labor Residency with the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) once in the Dominican Republic.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must provide proof of the extension or renewal of the employment contract.
benefits: Allows legal entry into the Dominican Republic for employment purposes.
Grants authorization to work for a specific employer in the Dominican Republic.
Serves as the initial step towards obtaining a temporary worker residency permit.
Renewable for extended employment periods.
Provides a regulated framework for foreign workers in the Dominican Republic.
required_documents: Completed temporary worker visa application form.
Passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months, along with a complete copy.
Inextensive Birth Certificate, apostilled or legalized as appropriate.
Two (2) recent photographs, 2x2 inches, front view, white background, no accessories, ears visible.
Certificate of No Criminal Record from the country of origin or any country of residence in the last five (5) years, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish.
Original employment contract and Resolution from the Ministry of Labor authorizing its registration.
Constitutive documents of the contracting company, copy of its RNC (tax registration number), and Internal Tax Certification (DGI).
Letter from the employing company committing to comply with labor conditions, information, transport, travel, and repatriation costs.
Surety bond for insurance to cover medical and repatriation expenses.
Medical certificate (receipt of medical examination approved by the General Directorate of Migration).
Copy of national identity document from country of origin (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Secure a formal employment offer from a legally constituted company in the Dominican Republic.
The employing company must register the employment contract with the Ministry of Labor.
Gather all required personal and company documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated as necessary.
Submit the VTT application to the Dominican Republic embassy or consulate in your country of origin or residence.
Once the visa is approved and issued, travel to the Dominican Republic.
Upon arrival, initiate the application for the Temporary Worker Permit with the Dirección General de Migración (DGM).

visas.name: Student Visa
visas.description: The Dominican Republic Student Visa is designed for foreign nationals who intend to pursue formal studies at a recognized educational institution within the country. It grants lawful entry and the ability to reside in the Dominican Republic for academic purposes, providing a clear legal status distinct from a tourist visa.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals who have been admitted to a Dominican school, university, institute, academy, or other recognized educational institution and plan to undertake full-time or substantial formal study.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Beneficiaries of student visas, once in Dominican territory, have a period of 30 days to present themselves to the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) to formalize the procedures for their residency or temporary permit, completing any additional requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa must be renewed annually for as long as the applicant fulfills the required conditions and remains enrolled in an educational institution. Beneficiaries must register with the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) upon arrival.
benefits: Lawful entry and stay for formal studies in the Dominican Republic.
Ability to remain in the country for the academic duration, subject to migration compliance.
Provides a clearer legal position compared to studying on a tourist visa.
Possibility of later residence formalities linked to the study stay.
Establishes a structured immigration record for future applications.
required_documents: Visa application form, completed and signed (typed or clearly printed)
One (1) frontal passport-size photograph (2x2 inches or 4x5 cm), with a white background
Original passport valid for at least eighteen (18) months (some sources say 6 months, but 18 months is a common, more stringent requirement)
Acceptance letter from a Dominican university or study center, specifying the level of studies, institution, and program duration
Proof of financial solvency (e.g., bank statements, scholarship document, letter from institution financially supporting the student)
Medical Certificate confirming the applicant does not suffer from contagious diseases, issued by health authorities of the country of residence
Criminal Record Certificate from the country of origin or where the applicant has resided for the last 5 years, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish
Legible photocopy of National Identity Document of the country of nationality and residence card (if applicable)
Cover letter from the applicant addressing the Consular Section, stating the purpose of the trip and personal details
Birth Certificate, duly apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish if not originally in Spanish
Medical examinations conducted at institutions authorized by the Dirección General de Migración (DGM)
Curriculum Vitae, educational certificates or diplomas (for some specific cases)
application_process_steps: Obtain an acceptance letter from a recognized Dominican educational institution.
Gather all required documents, ensuring passports meet validity requirements and all necessary certificates are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish.
Complete the visa application form.
Undergo required medical examinations at DGM-authorized institutions.
Submit the application and all supporting documents to the relevant Dominican consulate or through their official visa portal.
Pay the application fee.
Await consular resolution; inactive applications may expire after 90 days.

visas.name: Family Reunification Residency (Reunificación Familiar)
visas.description: The Family Reunification Residency program in the Dominican Republic allows individuals with close family ties to a Dominican citizen or a permanent resident to obtain temporary residency in the country. This program aims to reunite families and facilitates the process for eligible foreign nationals to establish legal residence.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals who are spouses or children of a Dominican citizen or a legal permanent resident of the Dominican Republic, or those who can demonstrate direct family dependency.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Family Reunification Residency initially grants a temporary residence permit valid for one year, renewable for four-year periods. After five years of continuous temporary residency, applicants generally become eligible to apply for permanent residency. For spouses and children of Dominican citizens or permanent residents, it is possible to apply for permanent residency directly without first obtaining temporary residency for five years. After ten years of continuous permanent residency, further renewals are typically not needed.
visas.renewal_conditions: The initial temporary residence is valid for one year. Subsequent renewals are for four years. Renewal requires new medical exams, valid residence card, personal ID (Cédula), passport with minimum 18 months validity, new photographs, a Dominican criminal record certificate, an updated notarized letter from the guarantor, and proof of the guarantor's economic solvency.
benefits: It is one of the residency categories with fewer demanding documentation requirements in certain cases.
In some instances, it is not necessary for the applicant to demonstrate independent economic solvency within the country, as the sponsor assumes financial responsibility.
It offers a pathway to long-term residency and potentially permanent residency in the Dominican Republic.
required_documents: Visa Application Form (filled and signed).

Letter of application for the visa, addressed to the Consul, stating personal details, nationality, residence, current activity, and purpose of establishing residency as a spouse/child of a Dominican or resident. (Notarization not required for this letter).
One (1) recent 4x5 cm (or 2x2 inch) photograph, front-facing with white background.
Original passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months (some consulates require 18 months).
Copy of any current or expired Dominican visas and visas from other countries.
Copy of the entry stamp to the Dominican Republic (once in the country).
Inextensa Birth Certificate (showing full parental details), duly apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish if applicable, by a judicial interpreter.
Marriage Certificate or notarized declaration of common-law union (minimum 2 years), duly apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish if applicable.

Police Clearance Certificate from the country of origin and any country of residence in the last five (5) years, issued within 12 months, duly apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish if applicable (not required for minors).
Medical certification confirming the applicant does not suffer from infectious diseases.

Letter of Guarantee (Carta de Garantía) from the sponsor in the Dominican Republic, duly notarized and legalized by the Attorney General's Office, stating moral and economic responsibility for the applicant.
Proof of economic solvency from the guarantor (bank letters, bank statements, property titles, employment certificates with salary).
Migration guarantee insurance policy contracted with an insurer authorized by the DGM (for the residency application in DR).
Authorization from parents or guardian for minors, if the applicant is not a parent.
Copy of the sponsor's Dominican ID (Cédula) or residence card (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Contact the nearest Dominican Embassy or Consulate to your place of residence to obtain the required 'Visa de Residencia' (RS) for family reunification.
Complete the visa application form and gather all necessary documents as specified by the consulate.
Pay the visa application fee and submit the complete dossier to the consulate.
Upon approval, receive the RS visa in your passport and travel to the Dominican Republic.

Within 30 days of arrival in the Dominican Republic, present yourself at the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) to formalize the temporary residency application and undergo medical examinations at authorized centers.
Submit all additional documents required by the DGM for the residency permit, including the migration guarantee insurance.

visas.name: Ordinary Temporary Residency (Residencia Temporal RT-9)
visas.description: The Ordinary Temporary Residency (RT-9) program in the Dominican Republic grants foreign nationals permission to reside in the country for a period of one year. This status is renewable and is intended for individuals who wish to establish a temporary legal residence in the Dominican Republic.
visas.target_applicant: This program is designed for foreign nationals intending to reside temporarily in the Dominican Republic and integrate with the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five (5) consecutive years of holding and renewing the Ordinary Temporary Residency (RT-9), applicants can apply for a change of status to Permanent Resident (RP-1).
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable annually. For renewal, applicants must submit a renewal request letter, passport with minimum six months validity, original temporary residence card and ID, Dominican criminal record certificate, two photos, and a guarantee policy.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign residents may find it beneficial for tax purposes, particularly regarding income from sources outside the Dominican Republic. However, specific tax advantages like those for rentiers or investors are not explicitly mentioned for the general RT-9 category.
benefits: Legal right to reside in the Dominican Republic for one year, renewable annually.
Ability to obtain a Dominican driver's license and vehicle insurance.
Exemption from tourist card purchase for entry into the Dominican Republic.
Path to permanent residency after five years of continuous temporary residency.
required_documents: Passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months, including copies of the full passport, two copies of the main page, and two copies of the last entry stamp.
Residence Visa (RS) issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MIREX) through a Dominican consulate in the applicant's country of origin, and a copy of the entry stamp.
Inextensa birth certificate (showing complete data of parents), duly apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish by a judicial interpreter if applicable.
Four (4) recent 2x2 photographs, two front-facing and two right-profile, without jewelry or accessories, with ears uncovered and a white background.

Federal criminal record certificate from the country of origin or where the applicant has resided for the last five (5) years, duly legalized or apostilled and translated into Spanish by a judicial interpreter if applicable.
Marriage certificate, declaration of singleness, or proof of cohabitation, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish by a judicial interpreter if applicable.
Guarantee policy contracted with an insurance company authorized by the DGM (e.g., Seguros Reservas).
Medical examinations from one of the institutions authorized by the DGM.

Documents demonstrating economic solvency in the Dominican Republic (e.g., bank certificate with a minimum balance of RD$300,000.00 and bank statements for the last 3 months, vehicle registration, property title).
Personal identity document from the country where the applicant declares to have resided legally for the last 5 years, if different from the country issuing the criminal record certificate.
Certification of No Criminal Records issued by the Attorney General's Office of the Dominican Republic, if residing in the country for a period.
application_process_steps: Enter the DGM services portal (personal.migracion.gob.do).
Register a username and password in the system.
Select the 'LISTA DE APLICACIONES' option, then choose the 'LOCALIDAD-OFICINA' and the 'Residencia Temporal Ordinaria (RT-9)' service.
Complete all required information in the 'CUESTIONARIO INFORMATIVO PARA SOLICITANTE' and upload scanned documents in JPG format.
Make the corresponding payment for the application.
Undergo medical examinations at an authorized DGM institution within three days of payment and await results (approx. 10 days).
Deposit the original physical documents in person at the DGM office as per the assigned appointment.

visas.name: Temporary Residency for Religious Purposes (Religioso)
visas.description: The 'Temporary Residency for Religious Purposes (Religioso)', also known as RT-4, is a permit issued by the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) of the Dominican Republic. It allows foreign nationals to reside in the country for a period of one year to carry out religious or missionary activities. This residency is the initial step towards legally living long-term in the Dominican Republic for religious workers.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is intended for foreigners who wish to exclusively perform religious or missionary duties within the Dominican Republic, requiring affiliation with a recognized religious organization in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Temporary residency is generally the first step towards permanent residency. After maintaining and renewing temporary residency for a period (typically one year of temporary residence, followed by annual renewals), an applicant may be eligible to change their migratory status to Permanent Resident (RP-1).
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew the Temporary Residency for Religious Purposes (RT-4), applicants must provide a letter of request to the DGM, a presentation letter from their church/congregation, passport with at least 6 months validity, original and copy of the previous RT-4 residence card, two recent 2x2 photos (front, white background, no jewelry, ears uncovered), a criminal record certificate from the Attorney General (if applicable), a guarantee policy from an authorized insurer, and proof of their NM visa and last entry stamp. The renewal process takes approximately 30 days.
benefits: Allows religious workers to reside in the Dominican Republic to perform their duties.
Eliminates the need for a visa or limitations on stay.
Permits opening a local bank account and signing rental contracts.
Is the first step towards obtaining permanent residency in the Dominican Republic.
required_documents: Letter of application for Temporary Residency for Religious Purposes addressed to the DGM, signed and sealed by the corresponding church or congregation, indicating guarantee for the applicant and identification of the signatory.
Letter of presentation from the church or congregation the applicant belongs to, signed and sealed.
Original passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months.
Four (4) recent photographs (2 front, 2 right profile), 2x2 inches, without jewelry or accessories, ears uncovered, with a white background.

Federal Certificate of No Criminal Record from the country of origin or where the applicant has resided in the last five (5) years, apostilled and translated into Spanish by a judicial interpreter (translation must be legalized and apostilled if from abroad).
Guarantee policy contracted with an insurer authorized by the DGM (e.g., Seguros Reservas).
Original unabridged birth certificate, duly apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish if in another language.
Copy of the Residence Visa (RS) used to enter the country, granted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and copy of the entry stamp.
Completed temporary residency application form (available on the DGM web platform).
Informative interview questionnaire to be filled out online.
For dependents: Passports and birth certificates, duly apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish. If one parent applies, the other must provide a power of authorization.

Proof of economic solvency for the guarantor (Dominican or foreign with permanent residence), which can be a bank certification with a balance of RD$100,000.00 or more with six months of movements, a fixed-term bank certificate, vehicle registration (year 2000 or newer, active, no opposition/exemption), or property title (sole name, no mortgage objection). A sworn declaration of solvency by the guarantor with two witnesses and copies of their IDs is also an option.
application_process_steps: Obtain a Residence Visa (RS) for religious purposes from a Dominican Republic consulate in your country of origin.
Travel to the Dominican Republic with the Residence Visa (RS) within its validity period (usually 60 days).
Register on the DGM service portal (personal.migracion.gob.do), complete the informational questionnaire, and select the 'Temporary Residency for Religious (RT-4)' service.
Upload all required documents in JPG format to the online system.
Pay the application fees, which include the dossier deposit (RD$14,000.00) and medical examination fees (RD$6,300.00).
Undergo a mandatory medical exam at the DGM's foreign affairs department.

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Rentista visa: proof of $1,500/month passive income
- Retirement visa available with pension documentation
- Real estate investment can qualify for residency

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A child born to a Dominican citizen in another country is a Dominican national and is entitled to citizenship. The choice of Dominican citizenship is optional and not automatic; it requires an intentional act by the person upon reaching the age of eighteen or after, including filing formal papers. Required documents include original birth certificates of the applicant and the Dominican parent(s), and a copy of the parent's Dominican identification card.

Naturalization.desc: Foreign nationals with Permanent or Investment Residency status may apply for citizenship after prescribed waiting periods. Generally, naturalization requires holding temporary residence for 5 years, followed by 2 years of permanent residency, totaling 7 years of legal residence. However, some sources indicate eligibility after 2 years of permanent residence. Applicants must be at least 18 (or 16 if married/authorized), have a clean police record, demonstrate financial solvency, and pass a Spanish language and civics test.

Birthright.desc: The Dominican Republic's stance on birthright citizenship (jus soli) has undergone significant changes. In 2010, the constitution was amended to weaken the concept of jus soli. In 2013, the Constitutional Court retroactively applied this change to 1929, effectively stripping citizenship from thousands of individuals born in the Dominican Republic to undocumented migrants, primarily those of Haitian descent. Currently, the 2015 Constitution specifies that those entitled to birthright nationality are those born within the territory who are not children of diplomats, illegal aliens, or foreigners in transit, or those born abroad to a Dominican parent who choose Dominican nationality upon reaching 18.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign national legally married to a Dominican citizen may apply for citizenship after six months of marriage, provided they hold valid Dominican residency status and have completed at least the first renewal of their residency permit. The marriage certificate needs to be authenticated and translated, and the Dominican spouse's birth certificate and Cédula are required. Applicants will undergo an interview and may need to take a naturalization exam.

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax (ISR):** The Dominican Republic uses a progressive tax system on Dominican-sourced income. For 2026, tax brackets are: DOP 0-416,220 (0% tax-free), DOP 416,221-624,329 (15% on excess), DOP 624,330-867,123 (20% on excess), and above DOP 867,123 (25% on excess).
- **Tax Residency:** Anyone staying in the Dominican Republic for more than 182 days per year is considered a tax resident and is liable for income tax.
- **Foreign-Source Income:** Generally, foreign-source income is not taxed for the first three years of residency. However, those with Pensionado (retiree) or Rentista (investor) visas under Law 171-07 are exempt from foreign income tax for an unlimited period.
- **Corporate Tax Rate:** The standard corporate tax rate is 27%.
- **Value Added Tax (VAT):** A standard rate of 18% applies to goods and services, with monthly filing.
- **Real Estate Property Tax (IPI):** 1% on value above RD$10,190,833, due March 11 and September 11, with a 50% exemption under special incentives.
- **Social Security Tax:** Employees contribute 5.91% and employers around 15.39% plus risk coverage, totaling roughly 21.3% of an employee's salary.
- **Incentives for Pensioners and Rentiers (Law 171-07):** These include transfer tax relief on the first property purchase, 50% IPI and mortgage tax reductions, and partial exemption from import taxes for vehicles. Pensionados require a minimum pension of US$1,500 per month, plus US$250 per dependent, while Rentistas need to show at least US$2,000 per month in stable foreign-source passive income.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** The Dominican Republic offers a significantly lower cost of living, estimated to be 40-60% lower than the U.S. A single person can live comfortably on US$2,400 to US$3,200 per month in a good neighborhood, or more modestly on US$1,500 to US$2,000. Rent can be 75% lower than in the U.S.
- **Language:** Spanish is the official language and essential for daily life and integration, especially outside major tourist hubs. Learning Spanish is highly recommended for faster adjustment.
- **Safety:** Use registered taxis or trusted ride-hailing apps at night and stay in well-lit, busy areas, particularly in Santo Domingo and Santiago. Tourist police channels are available in resort zones. Crime rates are considered low in many expat-friendly areas.
- **Registration & Bureaucracy:** Registering for tax obligations requires obtaining a National Taxpayer Register (RNC) number. The process for residency and other administrative tasks can be slow and frustrating due to bureaucracy, requiring patience.
- **Utilities:** Unreliable electricity supply and frequent outages can occur even in desirable neighborhoods, and air conditioning can significantly increase electricity bills.
- **Traffic:** Santo Domingo experiences chaotic and sometimes dangerous traffic congestion.
